answer: Under the California CCPA, a consumer whose nonencrypted and nonredacted personal information is subject to unauthorized access and exfiltration, theft, or disclosure may recover statutory damages in an amount not less than one hundred dollars ($100) and not greater than seven hundred and fifty dollars ($750) per consumer per incident or actual damages, whichever is greater. The maximum administrative fine for each intentional violation is seven thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500).
